summary: The human-approved reconciliation preserves the root seed byte-identical as negative rejection evidence, but the official CARIN 2.2.0 examples cannot yet supply the required authoritative-synthetic positive corpus: Patient/Coverage are zero-error structural candidates with unverified synthetic classification, and the pharmacy EOB fails strict offline terminology validation.
decisions: The repository-root four-file seed remains byte-identical and provenance-bearing, but it is nonconformant/unsupported under the strict CARIN 2.2.0 boundary and may be used only as deterministic negative rejection evidence; it must never be repaired, filtered, rewritten, or promoted to a positive.

The strict baseline remains FHIR R4 4.0.1, hl7.fhir.us.carin-bb#2.2.0, HL7 FHIR Validator CLI 6.10.2, and the checksum-pinned dependency closure under -no-http-access and -tx n/a. Older/latest CARIN substitution, invented profiles, source rewrites, and fabricated terminology semantics remain prohibited.

The exact official Patient-Patient2.json and Coverage-Coverage3.json publication examples are byte-identical structural candidates: their SHA-256 values are 5126c680cdcb0ccd1d0c0c032b720f1a92224fff2f5bf3fa30ab7319e437a188 and e72295932c41b57291e0013dfb3e81d2ae37fbcf549090fdf14932a6fefc7d83, and each produces zero local offline validator errors.

Publication-example labeling and the package manifest's CC0-1.0 license establish example provenance and usage evidence but do not attest a synthetic generation method or no-real-person provenance. All three official candidates therefore have synthetic_classification=UNVERIFIED_AS_SYNTHETIC and cannot enter the approved positive-fixture partition until authoritative classification evidence is supplied.

The exact official ExplanationOfBenefit-EOBPharmacy1.json has SHA-256 46952eba56089a44272d2707c87accc5f16325ec8d91acdf7eed107a1080fe62 but is not an offline strict positive. The pinned local validator emits eight terminology errors: four CodeSystem-definition-not-found findings and four version-null-not-found findings whose available metadata names 1.0.2.

Publisher-generated validation-summary.json (SHA-256 39dfcb19c9e522e8e812778f327f22766c0405f53a10e6cfc550e1d33a48514e) and validation-oo.json (SHA-256 d214c310a03f88cc1384d76945417395a7ae92cee04d906c87c72e9f29d07aaf) record zero EOB errors and five warnings. This is retained as authoritative publisher-QA provenance but does not substitute for the approved strict offline validator.

The four affected pharmacy supporting-information slices have required NCPDP bindings. Their ValueSets contain no expansions/concepts, the referenced CodeSystems are content=not-present, and the package directs users to restrictively copyrighted NCPDP standards access. No usage-approved authoritative offline terminology corpus is available, so membership cannot be verified.

TERM-UNVERIFIED-001 may represent unavailable terminology only for extensible, preferred, or example bindings, or unbound preserve-only values. It may not downgrade errors on required bindings, fixed/pattern constraints, slices, invariants, or coding-version resolution. A publisher-QA adapter was considered and rejected because it would make unverifiable required bindings appear to be a strict offline positive.

Once both blockers are resolved, fully approved official standalone examples are the resource authority and deterministic project-authored homogeneous searchset Bundles may wrap unchanged positive resources. Derived envelopes must record exact parent hashes and recipe/version, must not claim official provenance, and assert transport/reference behavior only.

The declared source set remains the reference-resolution unit. Patient/Coverage links required for the bounded chain resolve exactly once across documents; profile-valid Organization references may be preserved as untrusted unresolved unsupported-target references and are never dereferenced or treated as organization evidence.

DATA-001 remains a versioned FHIR input/validation-result contract under contracts/fhir/data-001 plus independent fixtures/harness under tests/fixtures/fhir/data-001 and tests/data. It does not define an API, persistence model, backend service, frontend, Docker topology, cloud resource, or deployment.

Validation remains layered across provenance/classification, strict JSON, support/envelope, base FHIR, CARIN profile/terminology, reference/project invariants, and content isolation. Accepted positives require both approved synthetic classification and zero validator errors; publisher warnings and local warnings/information remain recorded.
FHIR/profile conformance and official-example status never establish coverage, payment, coding, fraud, clinical, payer-policy, beneficiary, provider, amount, or real-world correctness.

Only contract and testing impacts remain. Contract/test workers must not promote unverified-synthetic Patient/Coverage candidates, suppress the EOB errors, or create accepted envelopes before both classification and terminology/source blockers are resolved.

risks.description: Substituting publisher QA for the approved offline validator or downgrading required-binding errors would create a false strict-conformance claim.
risks.mitigation: Keep the task blocked and require zero offline validator errors for every accepted positive; preserve publisher QA only as separate provenance evidence.

risks.description: Obtaining NCPDP terminology through an unapproved source could violate usage rights or introduce unverifiable semantics.
risks.mitigation: Accept only an authoritative, exact-version, digest-pinned, usage-approved offline corpus after license review; otherwise obtain a different authoritative strict-positive EOB.

risks.description: Project-authored envelopes could be mistaken for official search results or alter their authoritative child resources.
risks.mitigation: Generate envelopes deterministically from unchanged strict-positive parents, record parent/recipe hashes, label them project-authored synthetic, and make no upstream-search or domain claim.

risks.description: Narratives, displays, identifiers, URLs, and references in official or root examples remain untrusted and may carry active or misleading content.
risks.mitigation: Keep content inert, never render/execute/dereference it, sanitize findings, and test content-isolation behavior independently.

risks.description: A partial positive corpus could be mistaken for completion and allow downstream work to assume supported pharmacy EOB ingestion.
risks.mitigation: Keep architecture status BLOCKED, leave contract/test work paused, and require a fully classified three-resource strict-positive chain before CONTRACT_READY.

risks.description: Publication-example labels, test-looking values, or CC0 licensing could be misrepresented as proof that the official resources are synthetic or unrelated to real people.
risks.mitigation: Keep synthetic_classification=UNVERIFIED_AS_SYNTHETIC, prohibit positive-fixture/envelope promotion, and require authoritative generation/no-real-person provenance independent of validator success.

risks.description: The root seed still lacks complete upstream acquisition, generation, and license/redistribution evidence.
risks.mitigation: Retain unverified data-card fields and benchmark-freeze restrictions; validator results must not promote provenance or usage status.

blockers.description: The pinned CARIN archive labels Patient2, Coverage3, and EOBPharmacy1 as publication examples and provides CC0-1.0 license evidence, but it does not attest a synthetic generation method or no-real-person provenance. Patient2 and Coverage3 are therefore zero-error structural candidates, not approved authoritative-synthetic positives.
blockers.suggestion: Obtain authoritative source attestation or equivalent approved provenance establishing synthetic generation/no-real-person status for the exact hashed examples, or select a different authoritative, conformant, usage-approved synthetic corpus without changing CARIN 2.2.0 semantics.

blockers.description: The selected official CARIN 2.2.0 pharmacy EOB cannot be validated with zero errors offline because its four required NCPDP bindings reference CodeSystems whose definitions are not present in the pinned closure, and no usage-approved authoritative offline NCPDP terminology corpus is available.
blockers.suggestion: Provide an exact authoritative CARIN 2.2.0 pharmacy EOB that produces zero errors under the pinned offline validator, or provide an authoritative, exact-version, digest-pinned, license/usage-approved offline terminology corpus that validates the unchanged official example without rewriting it.

notes_for_next_agent: Do not advance DATA-001 to CONTRACT_READY or resume contract/test implementation while this report is BLOCKED.

Do not modify dataset/, substitute another CARIN version/profile, rewrite the official EOB, create NCPDP definitions, normalize publisher warnings over local errors, or suppress required-binding findings.

Preserve Patient2 and Coverage3 as zero-error official structural candidates with synthetic_classification=UNVERIFIED_AS_SYNTHETIC, and preserve the root seed as byte-identical negative evidence; none may be promoted to the approved positive partition yet.

After both authorized blocker resolutions, rerun architecture, update contracts/fhir/data-001 and independent tests together, validate classification evidence and all positives with zero offline errors, and prove dataset byte identity before and after.
PLATFORM-001 owns runtime APIs, parsing/normalization, persistence/quarantine, authorization, size limits, application dependencies, and deployment; none belongs in DATA-001.
